hints: Think about what each test is for separately, the orange precipitate tells you one functional group family and the yellow precipitate tells you a more specific structural feature.
The 2,4-DNPH test is positive only for carbonyl compounds, so narrow your list to just the aldehydes and ketones first.
The iodoform test needs a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so check which of your remaining carbonyls actually contains that methyl-ketone unit.
walkthrough:
**Decode the 2,4-DNPH test**

This is Brady's reagent. It gives an orange precipitate with any aldehyde or ketone.

Test rule:
$$\text{carbonyl (C=O) + 2,4-DNPH} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate}$$

**Decode the alkaline iodine test**

This is the iodoform test. It gives a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ only with a very specific structure.

You need either a methyl carbonyl group, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, or a group that can be oxidised to it, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$.

Test rule:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}- + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3\text{(yellow s)} + \text{RCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Combine both clues and test the options**

To pass both tests, the compound must be a carbonyl AND contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$.

Propanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. It is a ketone, so DNPH positive, and it has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ unit, so iodoform positive. That fits both perfectly.

options.A: Ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, does give a yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2$ because it has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group which is oxidised in situ. However it is an alcohol, not a carbonyl, so it gives no orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. It passes only one test.
options.B: Methanal, $\text{HCHO}$, is an aldehyde so it does give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. But it has no methyl group at all, so it cannot form $\text{CHI}_3$ and gives no yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2$. It passes only one test.
options.C: Propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde so it does give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. But its carbonyl carbon is attached to H and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, not to $\text{CH}_3$, so it lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ unit and is iodoform negative. A common trap is thinking any aldehyde gives iodoform.
options.D: Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone so it gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. It also contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so it gives a yellow precipitate of triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, with alkaline $\text{I}_2$. It is the only compound that passes both tests.
